stories.h: Brymo urges Tinubu to name National Theatre after Pete Edochie
stories.p: Singer Brymo has called on President Tinubu to rename the National Theatre in Lagos after the late Pete Edochie, while saying Wole Soyinka does not deserve the honour. His remarks have sparked heated debate.
body: Singer Brymo has sparked a heated online debate after calling on President Bola Tinubu to rename the National Theatre in Lagos in honour of the late Nollywood legend Pete Edochie.
## What he said
In a video posted on Instagram on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, Brymo addressed the president directly, urging him to immortalise Edochie by attaching his name to the iconic landmark.
He also argued that Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, whose name has been linked with the National Theatre, should not receive the honour, and spoke critically of the writer.
## Background

Pete Edochie died in Enugu early on Wednesday at the age of 79, after a long battle with prostate cancer. Tributes have poured in from President Tinubu, state governors and colleagues across the film industry.
## How people reacted
Brymo's comments have sparked heated debate online.
more: Brymo wants the National Theatre named after Edochie.
He said Soyinka should not get the honour.
His remarks have sparked debate.

stories.h: Atiku challenges Tinubu to explain ₦1.44tn drop in oil revenue
stories.p: ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar has reportedly asked President Tinubu to explain a ₦1.44 trillion fall in oil revenue in the first half of 2026, citing Budget Office figures. His campaign says collections were far below target.
body: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has reportedly challenged President Bola Tinubu to publicly explain a ₦1.44 trillion drop in Nigeria's gross oil revenue in the first half of 2026.
## The figures

In a statement on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, by the director of strategic communication for the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku's campaign cited figures from the government's own Budget Office. It said the government collected ₦7.88 trillion in oil revenue between January and June 2026, well below its half-year target of ₦18.65 trillion, leaving a shortfall of about ₦10.78 trillion.
The campaign argued that the drop came even as international crude prices rose in the second quarter of the year.
## The other side
No response from the presidency or the APC campaign was included in the reports.
## Background
Atiku, who turned 80 on Wednesday, is the ADC's candidate in the January 2027 election. President Tinubu sent him a birthday message despite their rivalry.
more: Atiku's camp cites Budget Office figures.
It says oil revenue was far below target.
The presidency had not responded.

stories.h: Osun Governor Adeleke dissolves executive council ahead of second term
stories.p: Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has dissolved his State Executive Council ahead of his second-term inauguration. He thanked the outgoing commissioners for their service.
body: Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has dissolved the State Executive Council ahead of his inauguration for a second term.
## The announcement

The dissolution was announced on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, after a valedictory council meeting, according to a statement from the governor's spokesperson. At the meeting, Adeleke reflected on his administration's achievements and commended members for their service.
He praised the outgoing commissioners for conducting themselves with honour and integrity in their various roles.
## Background
Adeleke, an Accord Party chieftain, is preparing to begin his second term.
more: Adeleke dissolved the cabinet on Wednesday.
He thanked outgoing members for their service.
He is preparing for his second-term inauguration.

stories.h: NDC alleges attempt on life of Kwankwasiyya influencer Maryam Golden
stories.p: The NDC's Kano campaign council has alleged that four masked, armed men broke into the home of social media personality Maryam Golden on Tuesday night. It described the incident as an assassination attempt.
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign council in Kano State has raised the alarm over what it described as an assassination attempt on Maryam Golden, a prominent social media personality who promotes the Kwankwasiyya movement online.
## What the party says

In a statement on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, the council's director-general said four masked men carrying dangerous weapons broke into Ms Golden's home in the Rimin Kebe area of Kano at about 9pm on Tuesday.
## Background

The Kwankwasiyya movement is led by former Kano governor Rabiu Kwankwaso, who is now the NDC's vice-presidential candidate. The allegation comes amid growing concern about political violence ahead of the 2027 elections, following deadly attacks on NDC events in Delta and Edo states this week.
## The other side
No statement from the police on the incident was included in the reports, and no arrests were reported.
more: Four masked men reportedly broke into her home.
The incident happened on Tuesday night in Kano.
No police statement was reported.

stories.h: Bandits abduct six residents in Kaduna's Millennium City
stories.p: Suspected bandits reportedly abducted nine people from two houses in Millennium City, Chikun, Kaduna State, late on Tuesday, later releasing three. Six remain in captivity.
body: Suspected bandits have reportedly abducted six residents in the Millennium City area of Chikun Local Government Area, Kaduna State.
## What happened
The attackers stormed two houses at around midnight on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, shooting and breaking in before taking nine people away. Residents said they began hearing gunshots at about 11:30pm.
Three of those abducted, including an elderly woman and a mother with her toddler, were later released, leaving six people in captivity.
## Residents' fears
A man whose wife is among those still held said he feared for her safety because she has difficulty walking, and appealed for help to rescue her.
## Background

Kaduna has seen several kidnapping incidents in recent weeks, including a foiled attempt at a school in Zangon Kataf and the abduction of Boys' and Girls' Brigade members in Kachia/Kajuru, most of whom troops rescued.
more: Nine people were taken; three were released.
Six remain in captivity.
Residents are appealing for help.

stories.h: NDC says supporters were attacked in Benin as Obi arrived for campaign
stories.p: The Nigeria Democratic Congress has alleged that gunmen attacked its supporters and campaign vehicles on Airport Road, Benin City, as Peter Obi arrived in Edo State on Wednesday. It said one supporter was critically wounded.
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has alleged that its supporters were attacked in Benin City, Edo State, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, as its presidential candidate Peter Obi arrived for a town hall meeting and other campaign events.
## What the party says

According to the party, attackers who arrived in a pickup van opened fire on its campaign vehicles parked along Airport Road while supporters waited for Obi. A party spokesperson posted videos online showing damaged vehicles and bloodstains, and said one supporter was critically wounded and receiving hospital treatment.

In a statement, the NDC's National Publicity Secretary said the attackers also assaulted people in the crowd and destroyed buses, and described the attack as unprovoked. The party blamed thugs it said were linked to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
## The other side
No response from the APC or the police to the allegation was included in the reports.
## Background

The incident comes two days after gunmen attacked an NDC campaign event in Delta State, killing several people, and on the same day the House of Representatives warned that a state of emergency might be needed in Delta if violence continues. The NDC has also boycotted a security meeting called by the police chief.
more: The NDC says one supporter was critically wounded.
It blames thugs it links to the APC.
The APC and police had not responded.

stories.h: Tinubu holds rally in Maiduguri, orders fresh push against insurgents
stories.p: President Tinubu visited Maiduguri on Wednesday, where he commissioned projects, held a campaign rally and directed security agencies to step up operations against insurgents. He promised to turn security gains in the North-East into economic recovery.
body: President Bola Tinubu visited Maiduguri, the Borno State capital, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, where he held a campaign rally ahead of the January 2027 election.
## Projects commissioned
On arrival, the president commissioned two projects: a female lodge for National Youth Service Corps members and the Borno International Conference Centre.
## Security push

Addressing the crowd, Tinubu directed security agencies to intensify operations against retreating insurgents and promised support for the families of troops. He pledged that the peace gains recorded in the North-East would be turned into full economic recovery.
## Background

Borno has been at the centre of the insurgency in the North-East for more than a decade. Earlier this week, state officials revealed that eight soldiers and 13 construction workers were killed during the rebuilding of the Mayanti community, which Governor Babagana Zulum has now reopened.
more: Tinubu commissioned two projects in Maiduguri.
He ordered security agencies to step up operations.
He promised economic recovery for the North-East.
stories.alt: President Bola Tinubu in a green cap and glasses at a meeting

stories.h: Supreme Court affirms Ogundipe as ADC governorship candidate in Ogun
stories.p: The Supreme Court has recognised Dr Biodun Collins Ogundipe as the ADC's governorship candidate in Ogun State, overturning lower court rulings in favour of Jimi Lawal. It held that the party's own primary guidelines decide the outcome.
body: The Supreme Court has affirmed Dr Biodun Collins Ogundipe as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 elections.
## The ruling

The apex court set aside earlier judgments of the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which had recognised Jimi Lawal as the party's rightful candidate. A key issue was which body had the authority to collate and declare results in the ADC's primary. The court upheld the party's three-tier primary guidelines, set by its National Working Committee, as the binding framework.
## Reaction

Ogundipe welcomed the judgment with humility and gratitude, saying it was consistent with the Supreme Court's long-held position that political parties have the power to run their own primaries without outside interference.
## Background
This week, lower courts also voided the candidacies of the NDC's Ovie Omo-Agege in Delta Central and the APC's candidate for Bayelsa West.
more: The Supreme Court overturned two lower court rulings.
It upheld the ADC's primary guidelines.
Ogundipe called the ruling a victory for party autonomy.

stories.h: Wike asks to lead Tinubu's campaign in Imo and Kwara
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has reportedly asked President Tinubu and campaign DG Abdul'aziz Yari to put him in charge of the APC's campaign in Imo and Kwara states. He said he had already secured Rivers and the FCT.
body: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has reportedly asked President Bola Tinubu and the Director-General of the APC presidential campaign council, Abdul'aziz Yari, to assign him to lead the party's re-election campaign in Imo and Kwara states.
## What he said

Wike made the request at a town hall meeting with residents and members of his Rainbow Coalition in Gokana Local Government Area of Rivers State. He is said to have argued that his work in Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory was complete, and that he was ready to step in where the APC was struggling.
He reportedly said he had received reports of difficulties for the party in Imo and of divisions within APC ranks in Kwara.
## Background
Wike, a former PDP governor of Rivers State, leads a coalition of PDP members backing Tinubu. No response from the APC campaign was included in the reports.
more: Wike wants to lead the APC campaign in Imo and Kwara.
He says Rivers and the FCT are secured.
The APC campaign had not responded.

stories.h: Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto becomes first mother to win Miss Universe
stories.p: Jennifer Barreto of Puerto Rico has won Miss Universe 2026, becoming the first mother and first married woman to take the crown. The final was held in San Juan.
body: Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto has made history as the first mother to win the Miss Universe crown.
## The final

The 27-year-old was crowned Miss Universe 2026 on Tuesday, 24 November, at the grand finale of the pageant's 75th edition, held at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum in San Juan, Puerto Rico. She beat contestants from 115 other countries.
## A historic win

Barreto is married and has a seven-year-old daughter, making her the first mother and the first married woman to win the title. Her victory also gives Puerto Rico its sixth Miss Universe crown, ending a 20-year wait.
## The winning answer

In the final question round, she was asked what human value should never be lost as artificial intelligence grows. She stressed using AI responsibly and keeping human values alive through consistent actions.
more: She is the first mother to win Miss Universe.
It is Puerto Rico's sixth crown.
The final was held in San Juan.

stories.h: Reps urge Tinubu to consider state of emergency in Delta if violence worsens
stories.p: The House of Representatives has asked President Tinubu to closely monitor security in Delta State, warning that a state of emergency may become necessary if political violence continues. It also told the police to set up a special investigative team.
body: The House of Representatives has called on President Bola Tinubu to closely watch the security situation in Delta State, warning that a state of emergency may be needed if conditions keep getting worse.
## The motion

The resolution on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, followed a motion by Representative Benedict Etanabene, who pointed to a series of politically motivated attacks in the state. Lawmakers expressed concern that the violence was spreading fear and threatening peace among communities.
## Directive to the police
The House also directed the Inspector-General of Police to identify flashpoints across the state and set up a special team to investigate the attacks.
## Background

The resolution comes two days after gunmen attacked an NDC campaign event led by former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege in Uduere, Ughelli North, killing several people. Police have invited Omo-Agege and others for questioning, and the Inspector-General has ordered an investigation. Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori has called for everyone involved to be arrested, whatever their party.
more: The House says an emergency may be needed if violence worsens.
Police must set up a special investigative team.
It follows Monday's deadly attack in Ughelli North.

stories.h: Tinubu congratulates rival Atiku on his 80th birthday
stories.p: President Tinubu has congratulated ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar on turning 80, despite their rivalry in the 2027 race. He recalled backing Atiku's 2007 presidential bid.
body: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate and former Vice President, on his 80th birthday.
## The message

In a statement released on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the president said the milestone deserved recognition. He noted that despite their different political paths, he wanted to acknowledge the history they share and Atiku's contributions to Nigeria.
Tinubu also recalled supporting Atiku's presidential bid in 2007.
## Other well-wishers
Businessman Tein Jack-Rich was among others who sent birthday messages to the former vice president, praising his leadership and resilience.
## Background
The two men are now rivals in the January 2027 presidential election, and their campaigns have traded sharp words in recent weeks.
more: Atiku turned 80 on 25 November.
Tinubu recalled backing Atiku's 2007 bid.
The two are rivals in the 2027 race.

stories.h: CBN raises weekly dollar limit for BDCs from $150,000 to $1m
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has reportedly raised the weekly dollar purchase limit for Bureau De Change operators to $1 million to ease festive pressure on the naira. Banks have begun implementing the change.
body: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has reportedly raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, in a move aimed at easing seasonal pressure on the foreign exchange market.
## How it will work

Sources said commercial banks had started contacting BDC operators to set up arrangements for the new limit. Banks will act only as intermediaries between BDCs and the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, using a purchase tracking platform.
## Background

The change is a major relaxation of restrictions the CBN introduced in February. It comes as the naira has weakened against the dollar in recent days and the country's external reserves have fallen. The CBN this week kept its benchmark interest rate at 23%.
more: The limit rises from $150,000 to $1 million a week.
Banks will act as intermediaries.
The naira has weakened in recent days.

stories.h: Raheem Sterling given suspended jail term for dangerous driving
stories.p: Former England winger Raheem Sterling has been handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, after pleading guilty to dangerous driving. The court heard he was inhaling from a balloon while driving his Lamborghini.
body: Former England winger Raheem Sterling has avoided an immediate prison term after a court handed him a 12-month sentence, suspended for 18 months, for dangerous driving.
## The sentence
The sentence was handed down on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court. The judge said the 31-year-old had shown a conscious disregard for the safety of other road users.
## What happened

The court heard that Sterling drove his Lamborghini on the M25 and M3 motorways during the morning rush hour on 28 May. Witnesses told police they saw him weaving between lanes while inhaling from a balloon. Officers who attended his later crash found him in the passenger seat with two canisters of nitrous oxide.
## Background
Sterling, who most recently played for Dutch club Feyenoord, pleaded guilty to dangerous driving in September.
more: The 12-month sentence is suspended for 18 months.
He drove his Lamborghini on the M25 and M3.
He pleaded guilty in September.

stories.h: Lagos seals four churches over noise pollution
stories.p: The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency has sealed four churches in Ajah and Ipaja-Ayobo for persistent noise pollution. The agency said the enforcement was carried out on Tuesday.
body: The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency (LASEPA) has sealed four churches over persistent noise pollution.
## The churches

The agency said on its X account on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, that the enforcement was carried out on Tuesday. The affected churches are a Celestial Church of Christ parish in Lambada, Ajah; a branch of The Lord's Chosen Charismatic Revival Movement in Ipaja-Ayobo; God's Word Faith Ministries in Ipaja-Ayobo; and His Presence Redemptions Ministry International, also in Ipaja-Ayobo.
## Why
LASEPA said the churches were sealed for persistent noise pollution, in line with the state's environmental laws.
more: Four churches were sealed on Tuesday.
Three are in Ipaja-Ayobo and one in Ajah.
LASEPA cited persistent noise pollution.

stories.h: US Embassy and Lagos consulate to close for two days for Thanksgiving
stories.p: The US Embassy in Abuja and the Consulate General in Lagos will be closed on Thursday and Friday for the American Thanksgiving holiday. Visa applicants with appointments on those days should reschedule.
body: The United States Embassy in Abuja and the Consulate General in Lagos will close for two days this week as the US marks its Thanksgiving holiday.
## The dates
The US Mission in Nigeria confirmed on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, that both offices will be shut on Thursday, 26 November, and Friday, 27 November.
## What it means
Visa applicants, travellers and members of the public with appointments or enquiries at either location will not be able to access consular services on those days, and are advised to reschedule.
more: Offices close on 26 and 27 November.
Consular services will be unavailable.
Applicants should reschedule appointments.

stories.h: El-Rufai tells court he never tapped Ribadu's phone
stories.p: Former Kaduna Governor Nasir El-Rufai has reportedly told a Federal High Court in Abuja that he never intercepted the phone calls of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu. He opened his defence on Wednesday.
body: Former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai has reportedly told a Federal High Court in Abuja that he never intercepted the telephone conversations of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, and never asked anyone to do so for him.
## In court

El-Rufai opened his defence on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, before Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, after his no-case submission was dismissed in October. Led in evidence by his lawyer, he told the court that he had never owned equipment capable of intercepting calls and had no technical knowledge of how such interception works.
He also denied having any access to the NSA's communication networks or personal devices.
## How the case began
The case arises from remarks El-Rufai made in a television interview on 13 February 2026. He denies the charges.
## What happens next
The trial continues as El-Rufai presents his defence.
## 'Political rhetoric'
El-Rufai told the court that his 'tapped' remark was political rhetoric. The court later adjourned the trial to February to allow his defence to continue.
more: El-Rufai denies intercepting Ribadu's calls.
He says he never owned interception equipment.
His no-case submission was dismissed in October.

stories.h: Seyi Law admits his finances were better before Tinubu, but backs reforms
stories.p: Comedian Seyi Law has reportedly admitted that living standards have dropped under President Tinubu and that his own finances were better before 2023. He still defended the government's reforms, saying good policies take years to stabilise.
body: Comedian Seyi Law, a known supporter of President Bola Tinubu, has reportedly admitted that living standards have fallen sharply under the current administration.
## What he said

Speaking on a podcast hosted by Nedu, Seyi Law is said to have acknowledged that his personal finances were much better before Tinubu took office in 2023, and that it would be hypocritical to say Nigerians are not suffering.
## Still backing the reforms

He nevertheless defended the government's economic reforms, arguing that Nigerians would benefit in the long run. Comparing Nigeria with China, he said major national transformations often come with heavy early sacrifices. When the host asked whether that meant Nigerians must suffer greatly first, he said people must feel the pain of a policy before reaping its benefits, adding that good policies usually stabilise after 10 to 12 years.
## How people reacted
His remarks have sparked debate online.
more: Seyi Law says his finances were better before 2023.
He still backs Tinubu's reforms.

stories.h: Veekee James sparks debate after moving ₦4m scholarship over winner's reaction
stories.p: Fashion entrepreneur Veekee James has reportedly withdrawn a ₦4 million scholarship from a recipient at a graduation event and given it to someone else, after the winner's flat reaction. The move has divided opinion online.
body: Fashion entrepreneur Veekee James is at the centre of an online debate after she reportedly withdrew a ₦4 million scholarship from one recipient and gave it to another during a live event.
## What happened

The incident took place on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the graduation ceremony of fashion designer Prudent Gabriel's fashion school. James attended with her husband, Femi Atere. When a woman's name was announced as the scholarship winner, she is said to have responded with a reaction many in the room saw as flat and unenthusiastic.
James then intervened and redirected the scholarship to another attendee.
## The debate
Videos of the moment have sparked debate online about how she handled the situation.
## Recipient speaks
The woman whose scholarship was withdrawn has since spoken out about the incident.
more: The scholarship was worth ₦4 million.
It happened at a fashion school graduation.
Opinion online is divided.

stories.h: Benny Hinn urges Edo government to fix roads after Nigeria visit
stories.p: American televangelist Benny Hinn has reportedly complained about the poor state of roads in Edo State during his visit to Nigeria. He said he would raise the issue with the governor.
body: Televangelist Benny Hinn has reportedly called on the Edo State Government to fix the state's roads, after an unpleasant experience travelling on them during his visit to Nigeria.
## What he said

In remarks shared online, the preacher said he planned to meet the governor during his stay and hoped the meeting would lead to better roads. He added, in a light-hearted way, that the roads would need to be fixed if the state wanted him to come back.
## How people reacted
His comments drew attention to the state of roads in Edo State and sparked reactions online.
## Background
No response from the Edo State Government was included in the reports.
## The governor
Hinn's remarks were directed at the Edo State Government led by Governor Monday Okpebholo.
more: Hinn says Edo's roads need fixing.
He planned to raise it with the governor.
The state government has not responded.

stories.h: ADC tells Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over Kano governor's interview
stories.p: The African Democratic Congress has reportedly demanded that President Tinubu resign or face impeachment, citing Kano Governor Abba Yusuf's recent interview about the 2023 Supreme Court ruling. The ADC says it points to possible gross misconduct.
body: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has reportedly issued an ultimatum to President Bola Tinubu, demanding that he either resign or face impeachment proceedings in the National Assembly.
## Why the ADC made the demand

The demand follows Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf's recent Hausa-language interview, in which he spoke about a promise to rejoin the APC if the president did not interfere in his Supreme Court case over the 2023 governorship election. The ADC argued that the governor's remarks suggested a link between the court case and a political deal, and that this could amount to gross misconduct, a constitutional ground for removing a president.
## Background

Yusuf defected from the NNPP to the APC in January 2026. In his interview, he claimed that his former mentor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, sent him to make the promise to Tinubu. The Kwankwasiyya Movement has rejected the claim as false and said the governor offered no evidence.
## The other side
No response from the presidency or the APC to the ADC's demand was included in the reports.
more: The ADC cites the Kano governor's interview.
It says the remarks point to gross misconduct.
The presidency had not responded.

stories.h: NNPC says $2.04bn in crude oil proceeds is not missing
stories.p: NNPC has dismissed reports that $2.04 billion in crude oil proceeds linked to its former trading arm Duke Oil is missing. It says the figure is the gross value of 29 cargoes and that all transactions were properly accounted for.
body: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed reports that $2.04 billion in crude oil proceeds involving its trading subsidiary, formerly known as Duke Oil, is missing.
## What NNPC said

In a statement on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, NNPC's chief corporate communications officer said the $2.04 billion represented the gross value of 29 crude oil cargoes, not missing or unpaid revenue. The statement was titled 'Duke Oil cargoes are fully accounted for'.

The company maintained that all transactions under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme were properly documented. It said the apparent gaps in dollar receipts were due to the way the programme's settlements were structured.
## Background
Reports suggesting the money could not be traced had sparked concern online.
more: NNPC says the figure was the gross value of 29 cargoes.
It says the DSDP structure explains the gaps.
Reports of missing funds had sparked concern.

stories.h: Air Peace to start London–Owerri flights on 15 December
stories.p: Air Peace says it will begin direct flights between London and Owerri on 15 December, from both Heathrow and Gatwick. The route is expected to ease travel for South-East Nigerians coming home for Christmas.
body: Air Peace has announced that it will begin flights between London and Owerri on 15 December 2026, in a move expected to make it easier for many Nigerians, especially those from the South-East, to travel home.
## The route
The airline said in a statement on Monday that the new service would operate from both London Heathrow and London Gatwick airports, giving passengers more flexibility when planning their journeys.
## Why it matters

The launch comes ahead of Christmas and the New Year, when many Nigerians living abroad return home to spend time with their families. A direct route to Owerri, the Imo State capital, is expected to spare travellers the long road journeys from Lagos or Abuja to the South-East.
## Background
The announcement comes as domestic fares have surged ahead of the festive season, with some return tickets within Nigeria reported to have doubled in recent weeks.
more: Flights start on 15 December.
They will run from Heathrow and Gatwick.
The route serves South-East travellers.

stories.h: Petrol falls to ₦1,055 at Lagos depots as MRS cuts pump price
stories.p: Five Lagos depots cut their petrol price to ₦1,055 per litre on Tuesday, the lowest among surveyed terminals. MRS stations in Abuja have reduced their pump price by ₦70 to ₦1,295.
body: Petrol prices have fallen further in Nigeria's wholesale market as competition among depot operators intensifies.
## Depot prices
Five Lagos-based depots cut their ex-depot price of petrol to ₦1,055 per litre on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, the lowest rate among the terminals surveyed by a market tracker.
## At the pump
The cuts are slowly reaching filling stations. MRS stations in Abuja reduced their pump price by ₦70 to ₦1,295 per litre, although that is still well above the depot rate.
## Background
Prices have been falling for several weeks amid competition between Dangote Refinery and fuel importers, though motorists have complained that pump prices are slow to reflect lower wholesale rates.
## Lagos too
MRS has also cut its pump price by ₦70 in Lagos, following Dangote Refinery's recent ₦99 cut.
more: Five Lagos depots now sell at ₦1,055.
MRS cut its Abuja pump price to ₦1,295.
Pump prices are still well above depot rates.

stories.h: Porsha Williams engaged a year after divorce from Simon Guobadia
stories.p: Reality TV star Porsha Williams has announced her engagement to her girlfriend, hairstylist Patrice 'Sway' McKinney. It comes about a year after her divorce from Nigerian businessman Simon Guobadia.
body: American reality TV star Porsha Williams has announced her engagement to her girlfriend, hairstylist Patrice 'Sway' McKinney.
## The proposal

The Real Housewives of Atlanta star shared the news on Instagram with a black-tie video of the romantic moment. She said the proposal took place on 21 November 2026, after the couple had been together for about a year.
## Background
The engagement comes about a year after her highly publicised divorce from Nigerian businessman Simon Guobadia, whose marriage to the reality star drew wide attention in Nigeria.
more: The proposal happened on 21 November.
The couple have been together about a year.
She divorced Simon Guobadia last year.

stories.h: Nollywood legend Pete Edochie dies at 79
stories.p: Veteran actor Pete Edochie, famous for playing Okonkwo in Things Fall Apart, has died at the age of 79. His family says he died in Enugu early on Wednesday after a long battle with prostate cancer.
body: Veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie has died at the age of 79, his family has announced.
## The announcement

In a statement shared on Instagram by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, on behalf of the family, the family said the actor died at 12:30am on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, in Enugu, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. The statement, titled 'An Iroko Has Fallen', described him as a beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.

He is survived by his wife, Josephine Edochie, his children, including actors Yul and Linc Edochie, his siblings and other relatives. The family said funeral arrangements would be announced in due course.
## His life and career

Pete Edochie hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 before becoming one of Nigeria's best-known actors. His major breakthrough came in 1987, when he played Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority's adaptation of Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart, a role that brought him recognition far beyond Nigeria.

Known for his commanding voice and powerful screen presence, he became famous for portraying traditional patriarchs and kings in countless Nollywood films. He was honoured with the national award of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON).
## His final weeks

In October, during a visit to Ghana, he spoke openly about his declining health, saying walking had become difficult, and prayed that he would not become a burden to those around him. Just this week, actress Toyin Abraham and her crew knelt to welcome him on her film set, and he had spoken publicly about his son Yul days earlier.
## Tributes
News of his death has drawn an outpouring of grief from fans, many of whom described it as the end of an era for Nigerian film.
## Governor and colleagues pay tribute

Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah described Edochie as an institution and said his death was a personal loss for the state, which the actor considered his birthplace and first port of call. Actress Funke Akindele, who worked with him in the film Egg of Life, recalled growing up watching him play Okonkwo and said his words of encouragement had stayed with her.
## Tinubu: 'larger than life'

President Bola Tinubu, in a condolence statement from the State House, described Edochie as one of Nigeria's greatest actors and a founding figure of Nollywood, graceful and larger than life both on screen and in person. Joke Silva, whose husband Olu Jacobs died earlier this year, Toyin Abraham, Omoni Oboli and his daughter-in-law May Edochie were among those who also paid tribute, while his son Uche shared the last photo he took with his father.
## More tributes
Content creator Peller also mourned the actor, sharing a moment from their last meeting and expressing gratitude for the time they spent together.
## Genevieve Nnaji

Genevieve Nnaji, who worked with Edochie on her directorial debut Lionheart, shared a photo of the two of them and an emotional tribute, describing him with the Igbo term of endearment 'nnanyi', meaning 'our father'.
## 'Irreplaceable'
Veteran actress Patience Ozokwo described his death as an irreplaceable loss, saying he was deeply committed to authenticity and always made sure cultural details were portrayed correctly on set.
more: He died in Enugu early on Wednesday.
He was best known as Okonkwo in Things Fall Apart.
Funeral arrangements will be announced later.

stories.h: NDC boycotts IGP's security meeting, says its members are not safe
stories.p: The Nigeria Democratic Congress has reportedly refused to attend a security meeting called by the Inspector-General of Police, accusing security agencies of failing to protect its members from attacks. It blamed thugs it said were loyal to the APC.
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced that it will boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing attacks on its members ahead of the 2027 elections.
## The party's reasons

In a statement on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, signed by its National Publicity Secretary, the party said it no longer felt safe under the Nigeria Police Force and would not lend legitimacy to a security process that had failed to protect its members.

The NDC accused security agencies of failing to prevent repeated attacks it alleged were carried out by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). It pointed to incidents in Benue, Edo, Cross River, Enugu and Delta states, including what it described as an attempt to stop its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State.
## The Delta attack

The boycott follows Monday's deadly attack on the campaign team of the party's Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Ughelli North. stories.p: A Federal High Court in Abuja has reportedly voided Fidelis Agbiki's candidacy as the APC's Bayelsa West senatorial candidate. The court upheld claims that his name was missing from the party's membership register.
body: A Federal High Court in Abuja has reportedly nullified the candidacy of High Chief Fidelis Agbiki, the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Bayelsa West in the 2027 elections.

The petitioners raised two main objections to his candidacy. First, they argued that his name did not appear in the APC membership register submitted to INEC, meaning he was not a recognised member of the party. Second, they claimed he did not resign from a political appointment before taking part in the senatorial primary.
## The ruling
Justice Mohammed Garba Umar upheld the petition, finding that the primary breached the Electoral Act.
## Background

The judgment came on the same day a Federal High Court in Warri voided the NDC candidacy of former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege for Delta Central on similar grounds relating to membership registers. Pre-election court cases are common in Nigeria, and both rulings can be appealed.

stories.h: Canada resumes Express Entry draws, invites 1,999 for permanent residence
stories.p: Canada has resumed Express Entry draws, inviting 1,999 provincial nominees to apply for permanent residence on 23 November. It was the first draw under new ranking rules that reward Canadian work experience and high-wage job offers.
body: Canada has resumed its Express Entry draws after a short pause, issuing 1,999 Invitations to Apply (ITAs) for permanent residence to provincial nominees on 23 November 2026.
## The draw

According to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, candidates needed a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score of 673 to be invited, and must have created their profile before 31 July 2026.
## New rules

It was the first draw since major changes to the CRS took effect on 3 November 2026. Candidates can now earn extra points through a new Labour Market Integration Factor, which rewards Canadian work experience or a qualifying job offer in a high-wage occupation.
## Why it matters
Express Entry is one of Canada's main routes to permanent residence for skilled workers.

stories.h: CAS restores Senegal as AFCON 2025 champions, overturning CAF ruling
stories.p: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has confirmed Senegal as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. It overturned in full the CAF Appeal Board decision that had handed the title to Morocco.
body: Senegal are once again Africa's champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) overturned the decision that had stripped them of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title.
## The verdict

CAS delivered its ruling on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, reversing in full the decision of CAF's Appeal Board, which had awarded the title to hosts Morocco. With the verdict, Senegal are officially recognised as the 2025 AFCON champions.
## How it started

Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 after extra time in the final at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on 18 January 2026, with Pape Gueye scoring the only goal. During the match, Senegal's players walked off the pitch for about 15 minutes in protest at a late penalty awarded to Morocco, which was later saved.

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation then took legal action, and on 17 March CAF's Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match, awarding Morocco a 3-0 win and the trophy. The Senegalese Football Federation refused to accept the decision and appealed to CAS.
## What it means
The ruling ends months of legal uncertainty over the continent's top football title. Before the verdict, CAF President Patrice Motsepe had said the body would accept whatever CAS decided.
## Morocco to fight on

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation said it rejected the ruling and would challenge it through every legal channel available, citing what it described as procedural failures. Senegal star Sadio Mane welcomed the decision.
## CAF responds
In a short statement, CAF acknowledged the ruling and pledged to act on it. The trophy, medals and prize money were never taken back from Senegal during the dispute and will remain with the team.

stories.h: Court sacks Omo-Agege as NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Warri has voided Ovie Omo-Agege's nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central and ordered INEC to remove his name. The judgment came a day after gunmen attacked his campaign.
body: A Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, has nullified the nomination of former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections.
## The judgment

Delivering judgment on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa ruled that the NDC failed to comply with mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act in nominating Omo-Agege. The court directed INEC to remove his name from the list of senatorial candidates and barred him from presenting himself as the party's candidate.
## Why the court ruled against him

The suit was filed by Professor Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, who challenged Omo-Agege's nomination, his resignation from the APC and his eligibility to take part in the NDC primary. The court held that the NDC did not submit its membership register to INEC as required, and that Omo-Agege was still an APC member when he took part in the party's senatorial primary on 18 May 2026. The judge first dismissed five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC.
## Background
The ruling came a day after gunmen attacked Omo-Agege's campaign event in Uduere, Ughelli North, killing several people. The senator escaped unhurt.
## Omo-Agege to appeal

Omo-Agege rejected the judgment and said he had directed his lawyers to file an appeal immediately. He disputed the finding that his name was missing from the NDC membership register submitted to INEC before the primaries.

stories.h: CBN keeps interest rate at 23% despite slowing inflation
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has held its benchmark interest rate at 23% at the last policy meeting of the year. Analysts had warned that election-year spending could put fresh pressure on prices.
body: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 23%, maintaining a tight policy stance even though inflation has continued to slow.
## The decision

Announcing the outcome in Abuja on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, after the Monetary Policy Committee's final two-day meeting of the year, CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso said members voted unanimously to hold the Monetary Policy Rate at 23%.
The committee also left the corridor around the rate unchanged, and kept the cash reserve requirement for commercial banks at 45% and for merchant banks at 16%.
## Why it held

The decision reflects caution amid renewed pressure on the naira and uncertainty at home and abroad. Analysts had said the recent drop in inflation might not be enough to justify a cut, warning that spending ahead of the 2027 elections could increase money in circulation and push prices up again.
## What it means
Borrowing costs for businesses and households are expected to remain high for now.
more: The rate stays at 23%.

stories.h: FG disowns ₦100,000 family grant portal, warns Nigerians not to share personal details
stories.p: The Federal Ministry of Youth Development has said the widely shared NFSP ₦100,000 family grant website is fraudulent. It warned people not to submit bank details, passwords, PINs or OTPs.
body: The federal government has disowned a widely publicised ₦100,000 family support grant, warning Nigerians not to register on the website promoting it.

In a disclaimer on its official X account, the Federal Ministry of Youth Development said the website for the so-called Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP) was fraudulent and was neither authorised nor run by the ministry.

The ministry urged people to stop using the platform immediately and not to upload personal documents. It specifically warned against sharing bank details, passwords, PINs and one-time passwords (OTPs).
## Why it matters

The purported grant had drawn wide attention online in recent weeks, with many Nigerians rushing to apply. There are now concerns that some applicants may have already submitted sensitive personal information.

stories.h: Police probe reported break-in at William and Kate's Norfolk home
stories.p: Police are investigating a reported break-in at Anmer Hall, the Norfolk home of the Prince and Princess of Wales. The family were in Windsor at the time and are safe.
body: Police are investigating a reported break-in at Anmer Hall, the Norfolk country home of the Prince and Princess of Wales, on Monday night, 23 November 2026.

Intruders are said to have entered the property while Prince William, Catherine and their children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, were at their home in Windsor. The family were safe.
## About Anmer Hall
The ten-bedroom Georgian house sits on the King's Sandringham Estate and was a wedding gift from the late Queen Elizabeth II. The couple regularly use it for weekends and school holidays.
## Business as usual
The reported intrusion came ahead of William's visit to Downing Street on Tuesday, where he met the Prime Minister to discuss shared priorities, including homelessness.
## Two men charged

Police said they were called to Anmer Hall shortly before 6pm on Monday after reports of suspicious activity and arrested two men nearby. The two Albanian nationals have been charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site, and are due to appear before magistrates in Norwich.

stories.p: An Abuja High Court has ordered the preservation of up to $100 million allegedly held by the Nigeria Governors' Forum, pending a dispute over legal and consultancy fees tied to Paris Club refunds. The order does not decide who owns the money.
body: A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory in Abuja has ordered the preservation of up to $100 million allegedly held by the Nigeria Governors' Forum (NGF), in a dispute over unpaid legal and consultancy fees connected to the Paris Club refunds.
## The order

Justice O.C. Agbaza granted the interim freezing order on 19 November 2026, following an application by a lawyer against the NGF's incorporated trustees and 29 commercial banks. The order covers a single total sum of $100 million, about ₦135.6 billion, across the affected accounts.
## What it means
The order preserves the disputed money until the court hears an application for an injunction or makes a further order. It does not decide who owns the funds.
## The claim

The lawyer is seeking payment under an indemnity he says the NGF issued in December 2018, after the federal government paid $100 million to the forum to hold pending a decision on liability for professional fees. No response from the NGF was included in the reports.

stories.h: VeryDarkMan warns Tinubu over deadly attack on NDC campaign in Delta
stories.p: Activist VeryDarkMan has issued a strong warning to President Tinubu after gunmen killed four people, including NDC youth leader Efemena Umukoro, at Omo-Agege's campaign event in Delta. He said political violence could spiral out of control.
body: Social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM) has issued a fierce public warning to President Bola Tinubu following the deadly attack on an NDC campaign event in Uduere, Ughelli North, Delta State.

He warned that even people close to the president would not be safe if the cycle of violence continued, and drew attention to the fact that the attack happened in Delta State.
## The attack

Gunmen opened fire on former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege's campaign team on Monday, 23 November 2026, while he was addressing supporters. Four people were killed, according to his campaign, including Efemena Umukoro, an Urhobo youth leader popularly known as General Akima. Omo-Agege was unhurt.

Other social media commentators also condemned the killings, and Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori called for everyone involved to be arrested regardless of their party. The Inspector-General of Police has ordered an investigation.

stories.p: Iranian authorities have reportedly flogged singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team over an online concert she performed without a headscarf. Rights groups say they also received two-year bans on artistic work.
body: Iranian authorities have reportedly administered 74 lashes to the singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team over a concert she performed without wearing the mandatory Islamic headscarf.
## What happened
According to a human rights lawyer and monitoring groups, the punishment was carried out on Monday, 23 November 2026, at the prosecutor's office in the city of Qom.
## The concert

The case stems from a virtual concert Ahmadi recorded in December 2024 at a historic caravanserai in Qom and streamed on YouTube. In the video, which was widely viewed, she performed traditional Persian music with male musicians while wearing a sleeveless dress with her hair uncovered, defying rules that ban women from singing solo in public and appearing without a hijab.
## The sentence

A court found Ahmadi and four male musicians and crew members guilty of offending public decency by publishing what it called immoral content online. As well as the lashes, each of the five was reportedly given a two-year ban on artistic activity.

stories.h: US adds 24 more Nigerians to 'worst of the worst' deportation list
stories.p: The US Department of Homeland Security has reportedly added 24 Nigerians to its list of foreign nationals arrested for serious crimes, bringing the number of Nigerians on it to 157. The allegations range from fraud to drug offences.
body: The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has reportedly added 24 Nigerians to its deportation list, bringing the total number of Nigerian nationals named to 157.
## The list

DHS updated its 'Worst of the Worst' initiative on Monday, 23 November 2026. The list identifies foreign nationals arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for what it describes as serious crimes, and now includes more than 45,000 people.
## The allegations

The people listed face allegations ranging from drug and weapons offences and violent crimes to fraud and the misuse of public benefits. Many of the Nigerians named were arrested over alleged wire fraud, mail fraud or impersonation in states including Texas, Virginia, New Jersey, Georgia and Indiana.
## Background
Being named on the list does not mean a person has been convicted.
more: 24 more Nigerians were added on 23 November.
157 Nigerians are now on the list.
Most face alleged fraud-related offences.

stories.h: 15 APC supporters killed in road crash on way to Zamfara campaign flag-off
stories.p: Fifteen APC supporters died in a road crash while travelling from Gummi to the party's campaign flag-off in Talata-Mafara, Zamfara State. The party has called off a rally planned for Maru.
body: More than ten members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) have reportedly died in a road crash in Zamfara State, shortly after attending the party's governorship campaign flag-off in Talata-Mafara.
## What happened
The victims were travelling back to Gummi Local Government Area after the rally when the accident occurred. Several other people were injured.
## Government response

Zamfara's Commissioner for Information and Culture confirmed the deaths in a statement on Monday, 23 November 2026, and said the state government had sent condolences to the victims' families and the wider APC family. As a mark of respect, the government announced the suspension of a campaign rally.
## Background
The tragedy came on the same day that four people were killed in an attack on an NDC campaign event in Delta State.
## Toll rises to 15

The APC's Zamfara campaign council later put the death toll at 15, saying the victims were travelling from Gummi to Talata-Mafara for the flag-off when the crash happened. It called off a rally planned for Maru Local Government Area on Tuesday as a mark of respect, and pledged support for the injured and the bereaved families.
more: The victims were returning to Gummi.
Several others were injured.
A campaign rally has been suspended.

stories.h: INEC warns 'rig and die' slogan could endanger polling staff and voters
stories.p: INEC has cautioned politicians and supporters against the popular 'rig and die' slogan ahead of 2027. A national commissioner said linking an electoral offence to death could incite mob attacks at polling units.
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned political actors and their supporters against using the slogan 'rig and die' ahead of the 2027 general elections.
## What INEC said

Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, at a media engagement in Abuja on ethical election reporting, National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna, represented by an INEC official, said that whatever its originators intended, a slogan that links an electoral offence to death is dangerous. He warned that it could encourage mob attacks at voting centres.
## Who is at risk
The commissioner reportedly stressed that ordinary voters and ad-hoc election staff at polling units, rather than senior politicians, are the most physically exposed if such slogans lead to violence.
## Background

The phrase has become widely repeated on social media and at rallies, with some saying it is aimed only at those who would rig the vote. INEC's warning comes amid growing concern about election-related violence, including Monday's deadly attack on an NDC campaign event in Delta State.
more: INEC says the slogan could incite mob attacks.
Polling staff and voters are most at risk.
The slogan is widely used online and at rallies.

stories.h: Tinubu formally declares for second term, claims Otti and four South-East states back him
stories.p: At a town hall with Igbo leaders in Lagos, President Tinubu formally declared he is seeking a second term. He also claimed Imo, Enugu, Ebonyi and Anambra, as well as Abia Governor Alex Otti, are with him.
body: President Bola Tinubu has formally declared his intention to seek a second term, while claiming the support of Abia State Governor Alex Otti and four South-East states.
## The declaration

Tinubu spoke on Monday, 23 November 2026, at a town hall meeting with Igbo leaders, traders and youths, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts in Iganmu, Lagos. He said the constitution allowed him to ask for a second term and that he wanted one, adding that the large turnout made him happy.
He framed his appeal around national unity, saying no Nigerian chose their ethnicity and all citizens share a common destiny.
## The South-East claim

The president listed Imo, Enugu, Ebonyi and Anambra as states he said were firmly behind him, and singled out Governor Otti, who was elected on the Labour Party platform, as a supporter. He said the absence of some of those he named from the event should not be read as displeasure.
## The other side
No response from Governor Otti was included in the reports. The South-East is widely regarded as a stronghold of the NDC's Peter Obi, who is from Anambra State.
more: Tinubu formally declared at a town hall in Lagos.
He claimed four South-East states and Otti back him.
Otti had not responded in the reports.

stories.h: Wike mocks Peter Obi's 'Obi Kererenke' chant in viral video
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has reportedly been filmed singing and dancing to the 'Obi Kererenke' chant while ridiculing Peter Obi's supporters. He described it as a children's rain song.
body: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has drawn attention online after a video showed him singing and dancing to 'Obi Kererenke', a popular chant used by supporters of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi.
## What he said

In the clip, Wike is said to have mocked the excitement around the tune, recalling that it was simply a song children sang while playing in the rain. He reportedly ridiculed the idea that it could carry Obi to the presidency.
## Background

The video follows recent remarks by Wike at events in Rivers State, where he repeatedly downplayed Obi's chances in 2027 and claimed he had neutralised the 'Obi Kererenke' wave. Wike, a former PDP governor, is now one of President Bola Tinubu's leading backers.
## The other side
No response from Obi or the NDC was included in the reports.

stories.h: Eguavoen reportedly tipped to take interim charge of Super Eagles as Chelle's deal nears end
stories.p: Augustine Eguavoen is reportedly the leading candidate to take temporary charge of the Super Eagles in early 2027. Eric Chelle's contract runs out in January, and the NFF's interim committee cannot sign long-term deals.
body: Former Super Eagles captain and coach Augustine Eguavoen is reportedly emerging as the leading candidate to take interim charge of Nigeria's national team in early 2027.
## Chelle's contract

Eric Chelle was appointed in January 2025 on a two-year deal that expires in January 2027. He had reportedly agreed in principle on an extension to August 2028, but the deal was never formally signed after NFF President Ibrahim Gusau and his board resigned and federation elections were postponed.
## Limited powers

A five-member FIFA Normalisation Committee is now running the federation until new elections, due by 31 May 2027. It is said to lack the authority to commit the NFF to multi-year contracts that go beyond its temporary mandate, leaving Chelle likely to leave when his current deal ends.
## Qualifying pressure
The uncertainty comes as Nigeria sit in a difficult position in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying group.
more: Chelle's contract ends in January 2027.
The NFF's interim committee cannot sign long deals.
Eguavoen has led the team on an interim basis before.

stories.h: Fire breaks out at Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith's Calabasas estate
stories.p: A fire destroyed a maintenance shed on Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith's $42 million Calabasas estate early on Monday. No one was hurt and officials said the cause was accidental.
body: A fire broke out early on Monday, 23 November 2026, at Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith's $42 million estate in Calabasas, California.
## What happened

Sheriff's deputies were called shortly after midnight when security staff reported flames on the 150-acre property. They found a maintenance shed fully ablaze. Firefighters spent about two hours putting out the fire, which officials said did not spread to any other buildings.
## No injuries
A sheriff's spokesperson said no one was injured and that the cause of the fire was accidental.
## Background
It is the latest in a string of fires to affect the family's properties over the past eight years. Their biggest loss came in January 2025, when the Palisades Fire tore through parts of Malibu.
more: A maintenance shed on the estate burned down.
No one was injured.
Officials said the fire was accidental.

stories.h: FIFA confirms US-led bid for 2031 Women's World Cup, UK to host 2035
stories.p: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, the first with 48 teams. The four UK nations will host the 2035 edition.
body: FIFA has officially named the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as joint hosts of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will host the 2035 tournament.
## The decision

The hosts were confirmed on Monday, 23 November 2026, at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress held virtually with representatives of its 211 member associations. Both joint bids were approved by acclamation, having been the only candidates.
## A bigger tournament
The 2031 edition will be the first Women's World Cup with 48 teams and 104 matches, bringing it in line with the men's tournament, and the first to be hosted across four countries.
It will be the third time the US has hosted the Women's World Cup, after 1999 and 2003, and the first time for Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica.
more: 2031 will be the first 48-team Women's World Cup.
The four UK nations will host in 2035.
Both bids were approved by acclamation.

stories.h: Four killed as gunmen attack Omo-Agege's NDC campaign in Delta
stories.p: Gunmen opened fire on former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege and his campaign team in Uduere, Ughelli North, Delta State, on Monday. His campaign says four people were killed and four others critically injured, and that the senator escaped unhurt.
body: Four people were killed and several others injured when gunmen attacked a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign event in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday, 23 November 2026.
## What happened

According to his campaign organisation, armed men opened fire at close range on former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC's Delta Central senatorial candidate, and his entourage while he was addressing a crowd that had gathered to welcome him. The campaign said the senator was not hit, although bullets passed close to him.
## The victims
The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation said four people died and four others were critically injured and receiving treatment. It named two of the dead as aides of the campaign.
## 'Assassination attempt'

In a statement by its media adviser, the campaign described the incident as a targeted attempt on the senator's life rather than a political clash, citing eyewitnesses who said the attackers made clear he was their target.
## What happens next
There was no word in the reports on arrests or a police statement. The attack comes as campaigns for the 2027 elections gather pace.
## Omo-Agege speaks

In a television interview on Monday night, Omo-Agege said the gunmen started shooting less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters, and that they shouted his name. He said a chance movement, stepping to the side of his vehicle to keep eye contact with the crowd, saved his life.
## Reactions

NDC chieftain Pat Utomi condemned the attack, saying violence would not cow Delta residents, and accused the ruling party of being behind political violence in the state. No response from the APC to that claim was included in the reports.
## IGP orders probe

On Tuesday, the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, ordered the Delta State Police Command to begin an impartial investigation. Preliminary police reports put the death toll at six. The police said the probe would also examine the conduct of officers deployed to the venue, and that anyone found culpable would be prosecuted.
## Governor demands arrests
Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori described the attack as tragic and said everyone involved must be arrested, whatever party they belong to.
## Who was killed
Among the dead was Efemena Umukoro, popularly known as General Akima, an Urhobo youth leader and one of the campaign's aides.
## Police invite Omo-Agege, others

The Delta State Police Command has invited Omo-Agege, the Ughelli North Local Government chairman and five others for questioning over the attack, as part of its investigation. Omo-Agege and the chairman are due at the State CID in Asaba on Thursday.
## Obi mourns
Speaking at a town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday, NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi led a minute of silence for the party members killed in the attack.
more: Four people were killed and four critically injured.
Omo-Agege escaped unhurt, his campaign says.
The campaign calls it an assassination attempt.

stories.h: Tinubu tells Igbo leaders in Lagos he was upset over 2023 votes but they have settled
stories.p: President Tinubu reportedly told Igbo stakeholders in Lagos that he was angry that some of them did not vote for him in 2023, but said the matter had been settled. He urged them to collect their PVCs and vote for him on 16 January.
body: President Bola Tinubu has reportedly told Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos that he expects their votes in the coming presidential election.
## What he said

Speaking in an informal tone at a meeting on Monday, 23 November 2026, the president acknowledged that some of those present did not vote for him in 2023. He said he had been upset about it at the time, but that both sides had since settled their differences.
He urged them to register, collect their Permanent Voter Cards and vote on 16 January, reminding them of what he described as an agreement between them, and stressing that he is the APC's candidate.
## Background
Lagos has a large Igbo population. The NDC's Peter Obi is among Tinubu's main challengers for 2027.
more: Tinubu said he was upset over 2023 but they have settled.
He urged them to collect their PVCs.
The election holds on 16 January 2027.

stories.h: Democrats win biggest US House majority in more than three decades
stories.p: US Democrats now hold 258 of 435 House seats after a recount in North Carolina, their largest majority since 1992. They also won the Senate in this month's midterm elections.
body: The Democratic Party has secured its largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than 30 years, according to media projections.
## The deciding race

US networks projected on Sunday, 22 November 2026, that Democrat Chuck Hubbard had defeated Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx in North Carolina after a recount requested by Foxx. The win gives Democrats 258 seats in the 435-member chamber, matching the number they won in 1992, the year Bill Clinton was elected president. Hubbard said Foxx had conceded and thanked her for her decades of service.
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries celebrated on X, saying the party now held the largest majority of any party in Congress this century.
## Senate too
Democrats also won control of the Senate in this month's midterm elections, a major setback for President Donald Trump and the Republican Party.
## What it means

Control of both chambers gives Democrats more power to block Trump's legislative agenda and launch investigations during the final two years of his presidency. The results were widely seen as reflecting voter frustration over living costs, tariffs and the conflict with Iran.
more: Democrats now hold 258 House seats.
They also won control of the Senate.
It is their biggest House majority since 1992.

stories.h: Medical academy urges Nigerians to take precautions against new COVID variant PJ.2.1
stories.p: The Academy of Medical Sciences of Nigeria has warned that festive travel and gatherings could spread a new COVID-19 variant, PJ.2.1. The WHO says the global risk is low and there is no evidence it causes more severe illness.
body: The Academy of Medical Sciences of Nigeria has advised Nigerians to take precautions against a new COVID-19 variant, PJ.2.1, warning that festive season travel and large gatherings could help it spread.
## What the advisory says

In a public health advisory signed by its president and the chair of its rapid response committee, the Academy said the World Health Organization has classified PJ.2.1 as a Variant Under Monitoring, while rating its additional global public health risk as low. It stressed that evidence about the variant is still limited.
## Where it has been found

The variant was first detected in Ontario, Canada, on 2 May 2026, and has since been reported in countries including the United States, Spain, France, the Netherlands, Israel, Singapore, Brazil, Argentina, Australia and New Zealand. WHO had recorded sequences from 18 countries as of 8 November.
## How serious is it?

Early studies suggest PJ.2.1, a descendant of the Omicron JN.1 family, may spread more efficiently than some other Omicron sub-lineages. However, there is currently no evidence that it causes more severe illness, and early laboratory findings suggest antibodies from updated COVID-19 vaccines can neutralise it.
more: WHO rates the global risk as low.
It may spread faster but is not more severe.
Updated vaccines appear to work against it.

stories.h: Thousands evacuated from Don Toliver concert in Manchester after unknown substance released
stories.p: Police declared a major incident at Manchester's Co-op Live arena after an unknown substance made concertgoers unwell during a Don Toliver show. More than 50 people were assessed and one was taken to hospital.
body: Thousands of fans were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live arena on Sunday night after an unknown substance reportedly made several concertgoers unwell.
## What happened

About 12,000 people were at a performance by American rapper Don Toliver, part of the UK leg of his Octane World Tour, when emergency services were called. Greater Manchester Police declared a major incident after reports of people falling ill in the crowd.
## The response

The ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, some of whom reported eye and breathing symptoms, and decontamination was carried out at the venue. Police said on Monday that several people were treated at the scene and one was taken to hospital.
## Investigation
Officers said they were working to find out what the substance was. The arena, which describes itself as the UK's largest indoor entertainment venue, said it was cooperating with the police.
more: About 12,000 fans were at the show.
More than 50 people were assessed.
Police are trying to identify the substance.

stories.h: APC says letter asking INEC to guarantee Tinubu's 2027 win is fake
stories.p: The APC has dismissed a letter circulating online that claimed its national chairman asked INEC to ensure President Tinubu is declared winner in 2027. The party called it fake and malicious.
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has rejected a letter circulating on social media that claimed to be from its National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, asking the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to guarantee President Bola Tinubu's victory in the 2027 election.
## What the letter claimed

The document, dated 22 November 2026 and addressed to INEC Chairman Professor Joash Amupitan, purported to ask the commission to use its administrative and operational machinery to make sure Tinubu was declared winner of the next presidential election.
## The party's response

In a statement on Monday, the chairman's special adviser on media described the letter as fake and malicious, and a calculated attempt to damage the reputation of the party's leadership and weaken trust in democratic institutions. The party said the letter did not come from Yilwatda or his office, and pointed to features missing from the document that would appear on genuine correspondence.
## Background
The row comes as campaigns for the January 2027 elections intensify.
more: The letter was dated 22 November.
The APC says it did not come from its chairman.

stories.p: President Tinubu reportedly asked activist Sunday Igboho to use his Iru Ekun Security Network to help protect lives and property in the South-West. The two met briefly in the president's car after the Ibadan rally.
body: President Bola Tinubu has reportedly asked Yoruba nation activist Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, to deploy his Iru Ekun Security Network to help protect lives and property across South-West Nigeria.

According to a statement released on Monday, 23 November 2026, by Igboho's media office in Ibadan, the two met briefly inside the president's official car after the APC presidential campaign rally at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, on Saturday.

The meeting is said to have focused on the work of Iru Ekun, a community security outfit founded by Igboho, and how its members could help reduce insecurity in rural and urban areas of the region.

Igboho is a well-known campaigner for Yoruba self-determination. The meeting took place on the day of Tinubu's campaign rally in Ibadan, where the president also met traditional rulers.

stories.p: Nigeria's High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has rejected social media claims that he was recalled or reprimanded. He said he was in Abuja for routine consultations.

body: Leroy Boseman, the father of the late Hollywood actor Chadwick Boseman, has died after a brief illness, according to reports.

The family announced his death in a statement, describing him as a beloved husband and father whose impact went far beyond his connection to a famous son. stories.h: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
stories.p: Nvidia's board has unanimously voted to bring back Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board member, weeks after he stepped down amid a controversy. The board said US government input assured it his return posed no national security risk.
body: Nvidia's board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and a member of the board with immediate effect, the company announced on Monday, 23 November 2026.
## The decision

The board said it voted unanimously after a series of discussions with Huang. It said it had received input from senior levels of the United States government and, based on that, was confident that his return posed no national security risk.
The board chair said Huang was the right person to lead the company and that his return was in the best interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers.
## Background

Huang co-founded Nvidia and built it into one of the world's most valuable companies on the back of demand for its AI chips. He stepped down earlier this month amid a controversy over his personal conduct.
## Shares surge
Nvidia's shares jumped 33% after the announcement. President Donald Trump backed the decision, saying he had been in contact with the board and had spoken with Huang.

The actress, who owns a church in Abuja, was seen praying and ministering to people at the gathering, fully immersed in the spiritual exercise.

stories.h: Abure-led Labour Party faction endorses Tinubu for 2027
stories.p: The Labour Party faction led by Julius Abure has reportedly endorsed President Tinubu for re-election. Abure said the faction would mobilise the votes the party won in 2023 behind the president.
body: A faction of the Labour Party led by Julius Abure has reportedly endorsed President Bola Tinubu for re-election in the 2027 general election.
## The endorsement

Abure announced the decision on Monday, 23 November 2026, after a meeting of the faction's National Executive Council in Abuja. The faction is said to have described Tinubu as the most suitable candidate to lead Nigeria beyond 2027, pointing to his political experience and his time as governor of Lagos State.
Abure also reportedly pledged to mobilise the six million votes the Labour Party claims it won in the 2023 presidential election in support of the president.
## Background

Earlier this month, Abure said he would not support Peter Obi, the party's 2023 presidential candidate, who is now running on the NDC platform. He had said he was open to working with either Tinubu or Atiku Abubakar, depending on how the party's leadership dispute was resolved. The Labour Party has been split by a long-running leadership tussle.
## How people reacted
The endorsement drew criticism and sarcastic comments on social media, with many users questioning the faction's motives.

In a television interview on Monday, Abure said promoting Obi as the party's candidate in 2023 may have been a mistake, and criticised Obi as unreliable over how he treated the party's leadership. stories.h: Infantino says Nigeria is not ready to host a World Cup yet
stories.p: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has reportedly said Nigeria cannot yet host the World Cup because of gaps in stadiums, airports and transport. He added that the country has the building blocks to get there.
body: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has reportedly said Nigeria is not currently ready to host the FIFA World Cup.

Speaking during his visit to Nigeria, Infantino was asked whether the country could stage a tournament of that size. ## Hope for the future

However, he reportedly did not rule out Nigeria's long-term chances, saying the country has the building blocks needed to eventually meet the standard. He also described the national training facilities he visited in Abuja and Warri as impressive.

South Africa remains the only sub-Saharan African country to have hosted the World Cup, in 2010, while Morocco will co-host the 2030 edition with Spain and Portugal.

stories.h: Tyson Fury reveals he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
stories.p: Former heavyweight champion Tyson Fury has reportedly revealed he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder after a severe mental health crisis. He speaks about it in an upcoming Netflix documentary.
body: Former world heavyweight boxing champion Tyson Fury has reportedly revealed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder after a severe mental health crisis.

The 38-year-old British boxer opens up about his struggles in an upcoming Netflix documentary titled Fury, which looks at his life, career and personal battles. It features interviews with Fury, his wife Paris and his father John.

Fury and his wife recalled how, after he was hospitalised with a suspected heart attack in June 2016, he began hearing threatening voices. stories.h: Jimmy Odukoya sues sister and Fountain of Life trustees over his removal
stories.p: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has filed a lawsuit at the Federal High Court in Lagos against his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and members of the Fountain of Life Church board over his removal as senior pastor.
body: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has gone to court over his removal as senior pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, filing a suit against his sister and several members of the church's board of trustees.
## The suit

The suit was filed at the Federal High Court in Lagos on Friday, 20 November 2026. Eight people are named as respondents, including his sister Tolu Odukoya, interim leader Pastor Rotimi Okpaise and other trustees.
The filing marks a significant escalation in the leadership dispute at the Ilupeju church founded by his late father, Taiwo Odukoya.
## Background

Earlier this week, the trustees announced that Jimmy had been removed because his appointment did not reflect his father's succession wishes, and released a 2021 video in which the late founder reportedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his successor. Jimmy has insisted his removal is invalid. A Lagos State High Court had already granted the trustees an order barring him from acting as senior pastor while their own suit is heard.
## What happens next
The court is expected to fix a date to hear the case. The trustees had not responded publicly to the new suit in the reports.
## Rousing welcome

At Sunday service on 22 November, Jimmy Odukoya received loud cheers and applause from the congregation as he arrived, despite the court order barring him from presenting himself as senior pastor. There was an unusually heavy security presence around the church.
## 'I have not been served'

Speaking to the congregation on Sunday, Jimmy said he had heard about the injunction against him but had not seen it or been formally served, so legally it had not reached him. He pledged to carry on with his ministry. The Lagos State High Court order was granted on 18 November, and the matter was adjourned to 1 December.
## Bishop Mike Okonkwo visits

Bishop Mike Okonkwo, who helped found the church, also attended a service and told worshippers the church had been battered on social media in recent weeks. He said he could not be separated from the Fountain of Life Church.
## Wife breaks silence
Jimmy's wife, Mo Jasmine Daniel, ended her silence on social media by resharing her husband's post after his Sunday welcome, a move widely seen as a show of support.
## 'Church is not a political party'

In a sermon clip posted on Sunday, Bishop Mike Okonkwo told worshippers not to take sides with Tolu, Jimmy or the board, reminding them that none of them died for them and that the church is not a political party.
## Court summons

On Monday, 23 November, the Lagos State High Court ordered Jimmy to appear on Thursday, 26 November, to answer contempt proceedings brought by the trustees. The judge allowed the trustees to serve him by substituted means, including newspaper publication, pasting at his last known address and electronic delivery, after normal service proved difficult.
